sn22.86:1.1: This discourse is also found at [sn44.2]().
sn22.86:1.5: This makes it clear that in this context, “realized one” cannot be just any sentient being. See note on [sn16.12:1.4]().
sn22.86:13.2: The particle _c’eva_ here has its normal role of slight emphasis in conjunctions, and so this phrase does not mean, “I *only* teach suffering and the end of suffering”. The point, rather, is that when he speaks of cessation, it is the cessation of suffering, not the cessation of an “existing being”. This saying is also at [mn75:16.1]() and [sn44.2:17.13]().
